headline_marked: [[Samsung launches Galaxy Card]] with up to 5% cash rewards, issued by Barclays on Visa
headline: Samsung launches Galaxy Card with up to 5% cash rewards, issued by Barclays on Visa
summary: The new credit card offers no annual fee, a recycled steel physical card, and applications open on July 22.
details: Samsung has officially launched the Galaxy Card, a new credit card aiming to compete with Apple Card. Issued by Barclays on the Visa network, it offers a physical card made of recycled steel and a virtual card provisioned to Samsung Wallet accounts.

Cardmembers can earn significant cash rewards, including 5% on direct Samsung purchases in the US, 3% on purchases made with Galaxy Card via Samsung Wallet, and 2% on streaming subscriptions. All other physical card purchases earn 1% cash back.

The Galaxy Card has no annual fee and no foreign transaction fees, though the annual percentage rate (APR) varies by cardmember. Rewards can be redeemed as statement credits or transferred to a bank account.
Additional perks include a 20% discount on Samsung's VIP Advantage membership and a $200 cash reward bonus after spending $2,000 in the first 90 days. Applications for the card will begin on July 22.

While optimized for Samsung devices, the physical card can be used by anyone, even those who switch to other smartphone brands. However, key perks tied to Samsung Wallet would be lost, with account management available via a BarclaysUS.com online portal.

Industry experts note that while the rewards aren't revolutionary, the card targets Samsung's loyal customer base and "card-maxxers." This move is seen as important for Samsung to enhance brand presence and loyalty in the competitive credit card market.
